about.title: Integration Guide
about.intro: CP OAuth supports OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code grants with secret authentication, plain PKCE and S256 PKCE. It is not a complete OpenID Connect provider: openid grants a user ID, never an ID token or JWKS. Metadata is available at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server; the previous /.well-known/openid-configuration URL remains supported.

flow.title: Authorization Code Flow
flow.description: The standard OAuth2 Authorization Code flow works as follows:
flow.step1: Your application redirects the user to our /oauth/authorize endpoint with your client_id, redirect_uri, and requested scopes.
flow.step2: The user sees a consent screen and decides whether to grant access.
flow.step3: If approved, the user is redirected to your redirect_uri with an authorization code.
flow.step4: Exchange the authorization code for an access token and refresh token via POST /api/oauth/token.
flow.step5: Use the Bearer access token to call GET /api/oauth/userinfo and retrieve scope-filtered data.
flow.step6: Refresh via POST /api/oauth/token with grant_type=refresh_token. Omit client_secret only when the original PKCE exchange omitted it.

endpoints.title: API Endpoints
endpoints.authorize_desc: Initiates consent. redirect_uri must match a registered URI exactly: HTTPS, or HTTP only on localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1]. Denial returns access_denied and the original state without requiring login.
endpoints.token_desc: Supports authorization_code and rotating refresh_token grants, JSON and URL-encoded scalar forms. Public PKCE grants omit client_secret entirely; empty or incorrect secrets are rejected. Refresh scope may only narrow the original grant. Tokens expire after one hour; refresh tokens after 30 days.
endpoints.userinfo_desc: Returns user data filtered by the scopes granted during authorization.
endpoints.revoke_desc: Revokes your application's access or refresh token (RFC 7009). The original grant controls secret authentication. Revoking a refresh token also invalidates all access tokens for that user/application; an unknown token returns 200. token_type_hint is only a hint.

pkce.title: PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange)
pkce.description: Public applications may use PKCE without a secret. Verifiers are 43–128 characters (letters, digits, dot, underscore, tilde, hyphen). S256 challenges are 43-character base64url SHA-256 values; plain is also supported and is the default method. Always send the verifier when exchanging a PKCE code. New grants exchanged without a secret can refresh/revoke without one; migrated grants still require the secret until reauthorized.

about.guide_intro: Register an application, complete the authorization code flow, and request only the data your application needs.
about.cookie_boundary: CP OAuth's own pages use HttpOnly session cookies and CSRF protection. Application integrations use grant credentials at /api/oauth/token and /api/oauth/revoke, and a Bearer access token at /api/oauth/userinfo. Do not use or forward the site's session cookie.

create.title: Register your application
create.description: In the developer workspace, enter an application name, register exact callback URIs, and choose whether users must verify their email before approval. Use HTTPS, or HTTP only for loopback development. The client secret is shown once after creation; save it securely if your server will use secret authentication.

credentials.title: Server-side secret authentication
credentials.description: Keep client_secret on your server, never in browser code. A secret-authenticated grant can be requested with or without PKCE; if PKCE was requested, its code_verifier is still required. An initial exchange that submits a secret makes that grant's refresh and revoke requests require the same secret. Missing, empty, or incorrect secrets are rejected.
